keyfacts: One hundred and forty-seven people were killed in the attack at Garissa University College in Kenya.
The dead included 142 students, three security officers, and two university security personnel.
Al-Shabaab terrorists carried out the attack.
The attack was Kenya's deadliest since the 1998 U.S. Embassy bombing.
Kenyan authorities have not released a list of the victims.
Kenyans used the hashtag #147notjustanumber to share the victims' stories.
The gunmen separated Muslims from Christians and killed the Christians.
The extremist group has also killed Muslims in recent attacks.
The Interior Ministry identified one attacker killed by security forces as the son of a government official.
The father of suspect Abdirahim Abdullahi is a chief in Mandera.
Abdirahim Abdullahi's father had reported his son missing.
Al-Shabaab is based in Somalia.
In 2013, militants attacked Nairobi's Westgate Mall, killing nearly 70 people.
Kenyan churches held Easter services under armed guard during mourning.
Churchgoers wept during Easter services nationwide.
An elderly man had reportedly taken a loan to educate his son.
The ETI claimed delaying CCS rollout could add around £1.2bn a year to meeting the UK’s 2050 carbon reduction targets.
The ETI called for a commercial CCS plant to be built in the UK.
The ETI said there is significant storage capacity off the British coast.
The ETI said no technical barriers prevent the use of CCS technology.
The ETI said no more than six hubs and 20 offshore stores would be needed to deploy CCS fully around the UK.
ETI programme manager Andrew Green said bringing CCS forward could reduce costs and risks to the UK’s decarbonisation pathway.
Andrew Green said long-term policy commitment from government is more important than early funding.
Andrew Green said the key to early cost reduction for CCS is deployment of investable projects.
Andrew Green said the challenge CCS presently faces is commercial, not technical.
Dr Luke Warren said the UK has been in a holding pattern on CCS strategy since the government cancelled the CCS competition in November 2015.
Dr Luke Warren said a UK CCS industry can be kick-started with modest sums of money pre-2020.
Dr Luke Warren said investing in CCS in key industrial regions can unlock decarbonisation across the economy.
Dipali Raniga said CCS provides the only way to lower carbon emissions for many industrial processes in a carbon constrained future.
Dipali Raniga said policy and support from government should be brought forward for CCS as a cost-effective solution.
The Treasury denied forcing Decc to axe the CCS pilot projects competition in late 2015.
Coron is in the province of Palawan, Philippines on Busuanga Island.
Coron is famous for its World War II wreck diving.
In September 1944, a fleet of Japanese ships were sunk in a raid by the US Navy.
About ten well-preserved underwater shipwrecks lie in Coron waters surrounded by coral reef.
Coron Island has many white sand beaches surrounded by large limestone cliffs.
Coron Island is the ancestral domain of an indigenous tribe managing it sustainably.
Tourism is the major industry in Coron today.
Quartiles divide ordered data into quarters.
Percentiles divide ordered data into hundredths.
The first quartile, Q1, is the same as the 25th percentile.
The third quartile, Q3, is the same as the 75th percentile.
The median is the second quartile and the 50th percentile.
The interquartile range (IQR) is the difference between Q3 and Q1.
A potential outlier is less than 1.5 × IQR below Q1 or more than 1.5 × IQR above Q3.
The five number summary includes the minimum, Q1, median, Q3, and maximum.
How to calculate median with even and odd list length.
A sensitive Environment Canada document was found on an Ottawa street.
A passerby gave the document to CBC News.
Every page carried the Protected B stamp.
The document detailed security vulnerabilities of the NEMISIS database.
Shutting down or hacking the database could affect prosecutions of lawbreakers.
Environment Minister John Baird asked government officials how the documents wound up on the street.
John Baird said the document was neither classified nor secret.
Paul Dewar said the security lapses raise serious questions about the government's ability to secure sensitive documents.
WP Engine informed customers this week that their credentials may have been compromised in a security breach.
WP Engine became aware of the breach on December 9.
The investigation is ongoing.
WP Engine is collaborating with law enforcement and a cybersecurity firm.
There is no evidence the exposed information has been misused.
Passwords associated with WP Engine accounts have been reset.
Many have complained about the lack of details from WP Engine.
WP Engine has promised to share information about the data breach as soon as it is available.
Founded in 2010, WP Engine currently has 40,000 customers across 133 countries, including SoundCloud, Yelp, AMD, and Britain’s Network Rail.
Findel has issued a profit warning for its full year figures.
Findel anticipates pre-tax profits slightly below the bottom end of predictions.
Findel's like-for-like sales for the period are expected to have risen by 10 per cent.
Phil Maudsley has been announced as Findel's new chief executive.
Phil Maudsley previously led Express Gifts.
Ian Burke will become Findel's non-executive chairman.
Tim Kowalski has announced his departure as group finance director.
Findel is an online retailer backed by Mike Ashley.
Federal Reserve notes are technically a debt that the Reserve owes the bearer.
Printing more money devalues the rest of the currency already in circulation.
The US government is loaned the very money it prints.
You cannot keep printing more money or the value of it will deteriorate.
Zimbabwe printed so much money that it became worthless.
The only reason money has value is because the US government says it does.
People accept USD because the US government is well-secured.
Fiat currency is a piece of paper that means nothing except what the government says it means.
